newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Oct 10.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning.
** India's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh heading for a hung assembly according to trends available from counting of ballot papers on Wednesday
** An interim anticipatory bail rescues former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao from arrest in a forgery case but the reprieve seen short-lived
** A 27-member National Conference government headed by Farooq Abdullah sworn in as chief minister of the troubled Jammu and Kashmir state. Promises to bring stability to region

** The steel ministry has assured sponge iron manufacturers that it would take immediate steps to increase customs duty on steel scrap to at least 15 percent from the existing five percent, according to a newspaper report.
** The government is planning to kick off the restructuring of the oil sector and move towards a market-determined pricing policy from the next budget, the Economic Times reports.

** Two recent moves by Tatas, India's largest business house -- a rights issue from Tata Sons and a decision to charge group companies for using the Tata brand name -- will help the group's holding company Tata Sons get closer to consolidation of its control over group firms and help ward off takeover threats, according to chairman Ratan Tata.
** Benchmark Bombay index closes 10.28 points or 0.52 percent up at 3037.63
** National Stock Exchange (NSE) index ends 0.82 points up at 874.72 with net traded value at 10.23 billion rupees
** Leading software firm Infosys Technologies says its 1996/97 (April-March) first half net profit rises to 141.1 million rupees from 80.1 million a year ago
The company says turnover for the first six months increases to 617.6 million rupees, posting a 58 percent growth
** Two leading auto firms Bajaj Auto and Mahindra & Mahindra to meet on October 31 to announce first half results for the six months ended September 30, 1996
** Truckmaker TELCO records 25.5 percent jump in domestic sales in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) to 93,552 vehciles against 81,260 units a year ago
